Platforms I deliver on

How I ran a 15-department CRM rollout

At William Everett I lead CRM delivery for a large public agency, taking 200,000+ records and 2,000+ users from scattered tools onto one system.

  1. Discovery

    Sat with leaders from all 15 departments to map how each one worked and where the old tools broke down.

  2. Requirements

    Turned it into user stories, acceptance criteria and compliance rules the developers could build against.

  3. Build and test

    Configured Salesforce objects, flows and permissions, then ran UAT with each department before go-live.

  4. Training

    Live demos, admin training, written guides and video walkthroughs for 2,000+ users.

  5. Adoption

    Moved support to self-service intake. Engagement rose 23% after launch.

How I use AI

AI is part of how I work every day. I use it to build software faster, I build it into products where it saves people real time, and I put guardrails around it so a person stays in control.

145screens shipped on one platform
3apps on the App Store

To build faster

I write the requirements, direct AI coding agents to build them, then review and test every screen myself. That's how one person shipped a full operations platform and three App Store apps.

Inside the products

  • Turns consultants' weekly updates into a monthly delivery report for directors.
  • Reads a business card and writes the follow-up in the sender's own voice, learned from their sent mail.
  • Turns meeting notes into tasks with owners and due dates.
  • Answers the agency's phone when the owner can't, and sends a summary of every call.
  • Sorts the inbox, flags what needs a reply and drafts one.

With guardrails

  • Nothing goes out without a person approving it. Drafts wait in a review queue with a daily cap.
  • Disclosures built in where the law requires them, like Illinois rules on AI in hiring.
  • A fast, low-cost model for sorting and a stronger one for writing, so costs stay predictable.
  • A plain fallback when the AI service is down, so the work never stops.
